_comment: THE SIX. The front of the platform: the front page and /sectors render these and
nothing else. Specified in eufabric-page-specifications.md §4.2, which is the
authority for this file — instances, sector edges, the boundary rule and the
rendering rule are all settled there.
WHY A NODE KIND AND NOT SIX SECTOR KEYS. The sector spine in data/sectors.json is
keyed on FIGARO industries because the input-output joins depend on that keying.
Hydrogen and circular materials are not FIGARO industries; a pseudo-key for either
would corrupt the join. So the ecosystem sits above the spine and points into it,
and an instance with no sector edge at all is a first-class instance rather than an
incomplete one.
THE FIELDS
id          the instance, and the tile's key. Never a sector slug: `chemicals`
spans two slugs and `batteries` covers part of one.
name        what the tile says.
icon        which drawing from the set in web/components/SectorIcon.tsx. Named
rather than derived from the id, because the icons are keyed by the
noun they draw and four of the six borrow a sector's.
sectors     the sector edges, [] where the instance has none.
sector_scope  a sentence, where the sector edge is WIDER than the instance.
Only `batteries` carries one today: FIGARO's batsol covers batteries
and solar, the instance covers batteries, and solar stays in the
register with no ecosystem edge. Null where the edge is exact — a
scope note on an exact edge would read as a caveat on a fact that
does not need one.
sectors_evidence  which pass or decision put the rows under that sector key, on an
instance whose sector edge was argued about. Added 15 October 2026 with
hydrogen's edge, and the same discipline data/sectors.json uses for a
child sector's `evidence`: an edge that took a ruling records what the
ruling rested on, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.
technology, project, measure, material
explicit edges, for the instances that have no sector key and are
DEFINED by them. Empty today for both: hydrogen and circular
materials have no dataset yet, and an edge list invented ahead of
the data would be the tile promising a page that does not exist.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. Carbon capture. It was on the first list of six and it is the one
entry that is not an industry: it is an abatement route several industries take, so
SUPERSEDED 15 OCTOBER 2026 BY GEORGE'S RULING: HYDROGEN CLAIMS THE SECTOR EDGE TO
`clean`. The evidence is that the hydrogen dataset has been keyed on sector `clean`
since brief 7 (PR #52) -- 66 rows, every one of them a hydrogen row, and the sector
key is where they have always lived. The paragraph below reasoned from the FIGARO
join and concluded the instance must carry no sector edge at all; what it got wrong
is that `clean` IS ALREADY A SPINE KEY WITH NO FIGARO CODE (data/sectors.json gives
it `figaro: null`, as it does `ccs` and `batsol`), so claiming it corrupts no join --
there is no join to corrupt. The edge was withheld on a risk that did not exist, and
the cost was a tile that opened a holding page while its hub was built and drawing.
WHAT THE EDGE CHANGES. The instance maps 1:1 onto a built sector, so
web/lib/ecosystems.ts `builtSector` resolves it and the tile opens /sectors/clean
instead of /under-construction/hydrogen. `sector_scope` is now required and carries
one: the spine labels `clean` 'Wind, heat pumps, hydrogen' and the instance is
hydrogen, which is the batsol situation exactly -- a sector key wider than the
instance, with the remainder staying in the register and carrying no ecosystem edge.
AND THE EXPLICIT `project` LIST IS EMPTIED, which is the edge's direct consequence
rather than a second decision. It named 22 of the 66 rows, and it existed because
an instance with no sector key had to enumerate its membership. The sector edge now
claims all 66; keeping a partial list beside it would mean the 67th hydrogen row had
to be remembered in two places, and the two would drift. Nothing on the site read
the list -- sources/check_sector_schema.py resolved the ids and folded them into the
same claim the sector edge makes, which is why the double claim never failed the
boundary rule: both claims name `hydrogen`.
Superseded 15 October 2026 by the paragraphs above:
HYDROGEN IS THE FIRST EDGE-DEFINED INSTANCE, and it is what the paragraph above
was written for. It has no sector edge, because hydrogen is not a FIGARO industry
and a pseudo-key would corrupt the join; its rows are filed under the `clean`
sector key, which no ecosystem claims by sector, and the instance names them one
by one in `project`. So the boundary rule is satisfied by exactly one claim per
row — the explicit edge — and `sector_scope` stays null because there is no sector
key to narrow. A scope note on an instance with no sector edge would be a caveat
on a relationship that does not exist, which is why the gate refuses one.
it is a technology node with edges from cement, steel and chemicals, and the CO2
transport and storage projects that serve them are shared project nodes.
THE BOUNDARY RULE, GATED IN sources/check_sector_schema.py. A project belongs to
the ecosystem whose product it makes. A recycling plant is circular-materials; a
recycled-content obligation on a producing sector stays in that sector with an edge
to circular-materials. Two ecosystem edges on one project fail the build unless the
project is flagged `shared` — which is what a CO2 store serving three industries is,
and what a plant making one product is not.
ORDER IS RENDER ORDER. Cement first because it is the one that is built; the rest
in the order brief 4 §2 lists them.

ecosystems.name: Chemicals
ecosystems.sector_scope: Organic chemicals and plastics. Fertilisers are excluded; ammonia and the fertiliser line are read under hydrogen.

ecosystems.name: Batteries
ecosystems.sector_scope: Batteries only. The sector key covers batteries and solar because FIGARO does; solar stays in the register and carries no ecosystem edge.

ecosystems.name: Hydrogen
ecosystems.sector_scope: Hydrogen only. The sector key is labelled 'Wind, heat pumps, hydrogen' and every row filed under it today is a hydrogen row; wind and heat pumps stay in the register and carry no ecosystem edge.
ecosystems.sectors_evidence: hydrogen dataset keyed on sector clean since brief 7 (PR #52)
